originalTitle: 对话李开复：别叫我们 “六小虎”，叫 “金钱豹”
title: A Conversation with Lee Kai-Fu: Don't Call Us 'Six Little Tigers,' Call Us 'Leopards'
oneSentenceSummary: In an in-depth interview, 01.AI founder Lee Kai-Fu reveals that after abandoning pre-training large models, the company pivoted to To B enterprise AI transformation services, achieving 250 million RMB in revenue in 2025 and over 1.5 billion RMB in orders for 2026. The company is preparing for an IPO and hopes to be called 'Leopards' rather than 'Six Little Tigers.'
summary: This article is an in-depth interview with Lee Kai-Fu, CEO of 01.AI, by LatePost. It details the company's transformation journey after abandoning pre-training large models in early 2025 and merging some teams into Alibaba. Lee Kai-Fu candidly shares the initial morale crisis, employee departures, and how he rebuilt team confidence through town hall meetings and securing the first major deal. The core transformation strategy is the 'Number One Project,' where Lee Kai-Fu personally acts as the 'Chief AI Strategy Officer' to open doors for enterprise leaders, providing a full suite of enterprise AI transformation tools based on Multi-Agent and ontology. The article discloses 01.AI's financials: audited revenue of 250 million RMB in 2025, orders exceeding 1.5 billion RMB in 2026, preparations for an IPO, and plans to become China's first profitable AI 2.0 company next year. Lee Kai-Fu also shares his views on the competitive landscape of large models, predicting consolidation among foundation model companies and emphasizing that the real opportunity lies in helping enterprises use AI to change their financial metrics.

mainPoints.point: 01.AI abandoned pre-training large models and pivoted to To B enterprise AI transformation services.
mainPoints.explanation: In early 2025, 01.AI transferred most of its pre-training and AI infrastructure teams to Alibaba, ceasing its pursuit of AGI. It repositioned itself as a To B company helping enterprises with AI transformation, with the core strategy being the 'Number One Project.'

mainPoints.point: The early transformation phase faced a severe morale crisis and employee attrition.
mainPoints.explanation: After the team restructuring, one-third of the office desks were empty, and the turnover rate was high. Lee Kai-Fu rebuilt team confidence through candid communication in town hall meetings and by securing the first major deal, ultimately weathering the most difficult period.

mainPoints.point: 01.AI has achieved rapid growth and is preparing for an IPO.
mainPoints.explanation: In 2025, audited revenue was 250 million RMB, with orders exceeding 1.5 billion RMB in 2026, nearly half of which is ARR. The company is dismantling its VIE structure, plans to achieve single-quarter profitability next year, and hopes to be called 'Leopards' rather than 'Six Little Tigers.'

mainPoints.point: The core product is an enterprise AI transformation platform based on Multi-Agent and ontology.
mainPoints.explanation: Products include a full suite of enterprise AI transformation tools and a dedicated management tool for top executives. The core is to help enterprises abstract their own systems so that AI can truly understand and assist in decision-making, ultimately changing financial metrics.

mainPoints.point: Lee Kai-Fu believes large models have zero stickiness, and the key to enterprise AI transformation lies in organization and culture.
mainPoints.explanation: He has not paid attention to model leaderboards for over a year and uses SOTA platforms to select models internally. He believes AI transformation can only be driven top-down, with bottlenecks lying in organization, culture, and strategic decisions, rather than pure technical capability.

keyQuotes: I hope in the future, people won't call us the 'Six Little Tigers,' but rather 'Leopards.'
If the market doesn't accept it, no matter how amazing the technology, it's worthless.
Only by getting big clients to sign contracts with real money can you go further.
If an Agent can't change one or more numbers in your quarterly report, it's just a vanity project.
01.AI is my greatest love and belief in the 45 years since my PhD—giving up was never an option.
